name: TCG 2010 (Edison era, Master Rule 1 baseline)
description: The DUEL_MODE_MR1 composite plus DUEL_0_ATK_DESTROYED, researched and confirmed against period (2008-2011) Konami rulebooks and an engine test for TCG play at SJC Edison (2010-04-24): two 0-ATK monsters still destroyed each other on a tie before Rulebook Version 7.2 (~March 2011) added an exception. DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION was investigated and deliberately NOT added: period research shows 2010 TCG Ignition Effect Priority was gated to the Summon response window specifically (not any chain resolution) while being unrestricted by location - a hybrid neither DUEL_OCG_OBSOLETE_IGNITION nor DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION reproduces exactly; this is recorded as an engine-level known_gap, not approximated by enabling the broader flag. See docs/research/edison-rules.md for the full evidence table and the correction record. Synchro Monsters are legal; Xyz/Pendulum/Link do not exist yet.

era.official_ruleset_label: Konami 'OFFICIAL RULEBOOK' Version 7.1 (current as of 2010-03-30, 25 days before SJC Edison; EDOPro calls the underlying preset 'Master Rule 1')

differences_from_modern.summary: The turn player may activate ignition effects with priority after a summon or chain end, restricted to the Monster Zone (OCG-style condition, part of the MR1 baseline). RETAINED AS A PROJECT-POLICY APPROXIMATION, not a claim that period sources prove it exact or objectively closest (see the known_gaps entry below): it correctly grants priority for a Monster-Zone ignition effect after a Summon, but wrongly withholds it for a Graveyard/other-location ignition effect after a Summon (e.g. Destiny HERO - Malicious - see Forum:Priority Q, which answers this exact scenario), and wrongly grants it after a chain resolves with no Summon at all. Kept over the two alternatives evaluated - no ignition-priority flag at all, and DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION - as a conservative compatibility compromise: it preserves the defining Summon-priority mechanic (for the Monster-Zone case) rather than deleting it outright (what the flagless option does), without expanding the privilege to every location after arbitrary non-Summon chain ends (what DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION does). This is a modelling judgment, not a measured/data-backed claim about which failure mode is quantitatively worse or more common, and denying a legal priority option (this flag's own failure case) is a real rules deviation that can alter duel outcomes, not a risk-free choice. See docs/research/edison-rules.md's Approximation choice section for the full three-configuration comparison and this framing in full.
The turn-1 player draws in their first Draw Phase.
Only one Field Spell can be face-up at a time.
A negated Special Summon still counts against 'only once per turn/duel' summon restrictions.

When two monsters with equal, non-zero-excepted ATK (including 0 ATK vs. 0 ATK) destroy each other in battle, both are destroyed - the 0-ATK exception ('neither is destroyed') was not added to the rulebook until Version 7.2 (packaged with Structure Deck: Dragunity Legion, TCG street date ~2011-03-04/08, ~10.5 months after Edison). Confirmed by an engine test that fails without this flag.

known_gaps.summary: Ignition Effect Priority: no existing ocgcore configuration reproduces the researched 2010 TCG rule exactly. Eight independently-dated contemporaneous threads from the same 'Yu-Gi-Oh! Ruling Queries' community forum (2009-06-10/11 through 2010-10-01, several bracketing Edison within weeks - independently DATED, not independently AUTHORED; two were located and are cited on the legacy Yu-Gi-Oh! Wiki/Fandom archive, while identical-content mirrors also exist on current Yugipedia; the other six are cited directly on current Yugipedia), a period-adjacent Konami OCG FAQ ruling for Destiny HERO - Malicious, and independently-converging modern community reconstructions consistently describe the immediate 'activate an Ignition Effect as Chain Link 1' window as gated to a successful Summon that does not itself start a chain, NOT to any chain resolution in general, while being unrestricted by the ignition-effect card's location (Graveyard-based effects qualified equally with Monster-Zone ones). The strongest single source (Forum:Priority Q, 2010-01-01) directly answers this exact scenario - Malicious used as Tribute-Summon material, then activated from the GY via priority - and states it applies to the TCG. No period-primary Konami/UDE document stating the complete rule in its own words was located; confidence is moderate-high, not absolute. DUEL_OCG_OBSOLETE_IGNITION (this profile's baseline, RETAINED as a project-policy approximation - see notes) is too narrow on the location axis (Monster-Zone only) though correctly narrow on the gate axis for the Summon case; DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION is correctly unrestricted on location but too broad on the gate axis (grants the window after ANY chain-end, including ones with no Summon at all); a bare configuration with NEITHER flag never grants the window at all, deleting the defining Summon-priority mechanic entirely (both Summon scenarios wrong, both non-Summon scenarios right). Confirmed empirically across all three configurations by an engine test matrix (tests/engine/test_historical_behaviour.py IgnitionPriorityMatrixTest, 12 tests). Representing this exactly would need a small ygopro-core change decoupling the single flag's two currently-coupled axes (event gate vs. location filter) into independently settable dimensions - not implemented here. See docs/research/edison-rules.md row 1 and the Approximation choice section for the full evidence, the three-configuration matrix, the retention rationale (a project-policy judgment, not a claim that period sources prove one configuration is objectively closest), and the correction record (an earlier pass in this same research had wrongly concluded DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION should be added; a later pass wrongly reported the Priority Q thread as not found).

Simultaneous Trigger Effect ordering (SEGOC): the period-primary Official Rulebook (2008-2011, bracketing Edison) describes a simple two-tier system (turn player's triggers first, freely ordered; then the opponent's) with no mandatory-before-optional split and no 'earlier trigger first' tiebreak - contradicting EdisonFormat.com's own claimed four-tier structure, which is only traceable to a 2012 forum thread whose participants assert (without period documentation) that it was already tournament-floor practice. Neither of the two specific mechanics DUEL_TCG_SEGOC_NONPUBLIC/DUEL_TCG_SEGOC_FIRSTTRIGGER implement (hidden-zone trigger folding; first-event-only restriction among several simultaneous events) is addressed by any period source found in either direction. Left unresolved rather than guessed; see docs/research/edison-rules.md row 9 for the full evidence and a candidate research lead (an unlocated later rulebook edition between Nov-2011 and 2017).

Three further candidate flags (DUEL_USE_TRAPS_IN_NEW_CHAIN, DUEL_TRIGGER_WHEN_PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE, DUEL_CAN_REPOS_IF_NON_SUMPLAYER) were researched but no period source (primary or otherwise reliable) was found addressing the specific behaviour in either direction - each rests only on an uncorroborated modern community claim or a card-specific ruling that doesn't clearly generalize. Left out of the flag set rather than added on unresolved evidence; see docs/research/edison-rules.md rows 2, 4, 8.
Extra Deck size limit for 2010 (15) is entered here from the EDOPro MR1 preset defaults, not yet from a period rulebook citation.

notes: Named -edison to leave room for splitting the long 'MR1' span into finer sourced eras later. As of the roadmap-item-5 research pass (docs/research/edison-rules.md), this is no longer a pure DUEL_MODE_MR1 profile: DUEL_0_ATK_DESTROYED was added on period-rulebook evidence and confirmed with a failing/passing engine test (tests/engine/test_historical_behaviour.py). DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION was investigated, found NOT to reproduce the researched 2010 TCG ignition-priority rule exactly (it overreaches into scenarios period evidence says Edison did not have), and deliberately left out as an engine-level known_gap rather than used as an approximation - this reverses an earlier pass's conclusion in this same research effort; see the dossier's correction record. Several other candidate flags remain deliberately unresolved (known_gaps) rather than enabled on name-plausibility or uncorroborated community claims alone; this profile should stay 'partial' in format.json's implementation_status until those are settled.
